title: The Gan–Gross–Prasad conjectures for classical groups: relevant pairs, Vogan packets, Bessel models and periods
summary: A shared framework for classical Gan–Gross–Prasad problems, from relevant inclusions and their Bessel models to local packet multiplicities, global period propositions and normalized unitary identities. The plan also connects the classical spectral geometry to distinguished tempered spectra, anisotropic automorphic averages and definite and arithmetic diagonal periods. It keeps conjectural assertions separate from proven ranges, tracks exact normalization and classification hypotheses, and imports trace-comparison, orbit-method and Shimura machinery from their owners.
readme:
This roadmap supplies the shared language of classical Gan–Gross–Prasad problems and the automorphic statements that use it. A nonzero global period must satisfy local distinction, coherence and automorphic occurrence; these conditions must be kept distinct. The local packet-count theorems, normalized period factors, spectral conductor comparison and arithmetic graph periods share the same relevant inclusions and dual conventions.

The local and global fields have characteristic zero. Hermitian forms and inner products are linear in the first argument. GN.2 uses the opposite hermitian convention, so its form is conjugated on import. A bilinear model for π⊠σ branches into σ∨; the sesquilinear branching period on π and σ has tensor parameter π×σ∨. Pure inner forms retain the complementary space, and even special orthogonal packets retain the supplied outer-orbit ambiguity. Completed L-values contain all archimedean factors; the removed-place notation always displays its removed set. The refined unitary constant uses the unquotiented sign group.

GGP.0–GGP.4 establish the framework, GGP.5–GGP.7 connect classical spectral geometry with distinguished spectra and anisotropic automorphic families, and GGP.8 gives definite and conjectural arithmetic endpoints. The local nonarchimedean generic and archimedean tempered ranges are stated precisely. The SO₃/SO₂ weighted-mean correction is retained, while the Weyl law and unrestricted weak-subconvex endpoint have their own scopes.

The source set comprises Gan–Gross–Prasad, Jiang–Zhang, Beuzart-Plessis, Gan–Ichino, Mœglin–Waldspurger, Luo, Harris, BPLZZ, BCZ, Nelson–Venkatesh and Liu–Tian–Xiao–Zhang–Zhu, with version-specific theorem and page locators below. This is a target-level plan, not a claim of formalization. Known global unitary proofs are supplied by JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison; quantitative operator calculus, relative-character sums and limit states by QuantitativeOrbitMethodAndMicrolocalAnalysisOnLieGroups; unitary Shimura models by their PEL extension. Those proposed suppliers need precise registered theorem exports, as recorded in the packet contracts.

The roadmap does not rebuild classical groups, compact branching, local/global Arthur classification, general automorphic or tensor-L-function theory, the global Jacquet–Rallis comparison, the quantitative orbit calculus, integral unitary moduli or cycle theories. It does not assert the general global or arithmetic conjectures, a real nontempered local theorem, an archimedean positivity theorem absent from the stated inputs, or Abel–Jacobi nonvanishing from Chow nonvanishing alone. Fourier–Jacobi models have no routed consumer in this pass and require their own oscillator-data extension when that scope is requested.

The arithmetic Chow graph contract includes smooth quasi-projective Shimura varieties; the projective-only MC.0 correspondence is used only in its valid subcase. U1 records the missing general cycle and Hecke interface.

stages.title: Relevant pairs and Bessel models
stages.description: Define odd-complement orthogonal and unitary inclusions, their relevant pure inner twists, flag characters and Bessel functionals in the correct local categories. Relate smooth models to twisted Jacquet modules and prove individual-model uniqueness, including split GL restriction.

stages.title: Packets, Hermitian parameters and base change
stages.description: Specialize supplied local and global packet classifications to relevant form pairs. Retain coherence, actual automorphic realizations, even-SO orbit conventions and generic-discrete cuspidality. Define Hermitian isobaric parameters, the unquotiented sign group and split-almost-everywhere weak base change, and compare the latter with strong base change only in its proven range.

stages.title: Local GGP propositions and known ranges
stages.description: Formulate the packet-count proposition and its unique-member equivalence. Establish the tempered nonarchimedean and real unitary, generic nonarchimedean orthogonal and unitary, and tempered archimedean orthogonal cases with their classification and analytic assumptions. Derive injectivity of transfer on the distinguished locus.

stages.title: Global Bessel periods and GGP propositions
stages.description: Construct the fixed Bessel Fourier coefficient and the bilinear global period, establish convergence with one cuspidal factor and local necessity, and distinguish fixed-realization from coherent-packet global GGP. Record the exact proven unitary and conditional descent ranges without reproducing their proof machinery.

stages.title: Local normalization and the unitary refinement
stages.description: Define the completed shifted L-quotient, the four-vector local branching form and its correctly dualized tensor form. Prove tempered convergence and the unramified calculation. Define normalized local periods and the unitary Ichino–Ikeda proposition, with Tamagawa measures and the actual component-group denominator.

stages.title: Classical spectral invariants and conductor dropping
stages.description: Define the adjusted eigenvalue multiset, retaining the even-SO Pfaffian. Prove isotropic eigenvector, regularity and geometric sphericity statements. Relate real Langlands parameters to infinitesimal character and tensor gamma weights; import spectral stability to identify the zero-weight obstruction to full conductor growth.

stages.title: The distinguished tempered spectrum
stages.description: Specify the smooth distinguished locus, period support, nonarchimedean positivity and phase normalization of branching maps. Establish injection of induction parameters and the explicit torus-component topology, with continuity and finite good-level truncations. Specialize existing compact decomposition to realize finite spectral weights.

stages.title: Automorphic families, means and weak subconvexity
stages.description: Specify actual automorphic embeddings and admissible spectral windows for anisotropic unitary and orthogonal pairs. Define the global branching coefficient and removed-place refinement. Prove the corrected weighted limit, family Weyl law, conductor–cardinality comparison, mean coefficient theorem and little-o subconvexity endpoint using the orbit-method supplier.

stages.title: Definite and arithmetic diagonal periods
stages.description: Specify the common relevant arithmetic unitary data. Define the finite graph-sum period, compare it with the compact global integral with the correct stabilizer weights, and prove the central-value definite nonvanishing endpoint. Define the derivative-to-Chow nonvanishing proposition while keeping it conjectural and separate from Abel–Jacobi nonvanishing.
